taglines: It is Father's Day and someone in your family sent a text that said 'happy father's day' and someone else responded with a gif of a bear waving and now the thread is just emojis and you are watching from the outside of this communication like an anthropologist studying a culture that uses thumbs-up to mean at least four different things.

Today is the summer solstice and it is also the longest day of the year and you can feel that. Not metaphorically. Literally the sun has been up since before you were ready and will continue to be up until after you gave up and the whole thing feels like a personal challenge from the solar system.

You have seventeen tabs open. Two of them are the same article. You bookmarked it before opening it again. You have not read it. You will not read it. It is about habits. It is about the one weird trick for building habits. You have a folder of bookmarked articles about habits. The folder is called 'READ THIS.'

Sunday is a social construct designed to make Monday feel inevitable. You have been resisting Monday since Friday afternoon and the resistance has taken the form of doing almost exactly what you would do on a weekday but slower and with worse posture and calling it rest.

The solstice means the sun is at its highest arc and will now begin its slow descent toward winter and somewhere a person who owns crystals is outside doing something about this and honestly good for them. Commitment to a bit is underrated.

You told yourself you would do something meaningful with the extra daylight. The extra daylight is now behind you. You used it to scroll with the lights off in a bright room which is technically different from scrolling in the dark but only technically.

Father's Day brunch is happening somewhere in your city right now. Eggs benedict. Bottomless mimosas. A man in a polo getting a card that says 'World's Best Dad' with a cartoon grill on it. He is going to keep that card. He is going to keep that card in a drawer and it is going to be there when they clean out his house someday and it will mean something enormous and it cost $4.99.

It is June 21st which means the year is almost exactly half over and if you were keeping score on the things you said you would do in 2026 the score is complicated and the complexity is the score and you should probably update your notes app about this.
